description: PAPL (Planner-Aware Path Learning) finetune of the LLaDA-style SQL masked-diffusion checkpoint. Goal: align training with the confidence-based decoding planner used at inference, to cut denoising steps (faster inference) at equal accuracy.

base_checkpoint.name: diffusion-sql-modernbert
base_checkpoint.training: 10-epoch LLaDA-style absorbing-state masked diffusion, 1/t-weighted CE, continuous t~U(1e-3,1] Bernoulli masking, on-the-fly augmentation
base_checkpoint.layout: [CLS] <PROMPT> p </PROMPT> <CONTEXT> c </CONTEXT> <SQL> sql+pads </SQL> [SEP]; SQL window = 128 tokens, max_len = 512

finetune_recipe.loss: ce_papl = ce + tau * stopgrad(exp(-ce)) * ce, then standard (1/t)*sum/SQL_WINDOW; tau=0 recovers plain LLaDA loss
finetune_recipe.loss_intuition: exp(-ce) ~1 when the model is already confident (low CE); those tokens are the ones the confidence planner commits first at inference, so PAPL trains them harder -> early commits more reliable -> trace more robust + model reaches high confidence sooner (early-stop fires earlier).
finetune_recipe.note: These are the A/B experiment settings, not a tuned prod recipe. The step gain was modest at tau=0.3/2-epoch (see ab_result); a tau sweep or 1-epoch schedule may improve it before final prod selection.

ab_result.summary: Same accuracy as the tau=0 control, ~5% fewer denoising steps (clean), consistent on augmented. PAPL did what it is designed to do; magnitude modest.
ab_result.eval: generation exact-match + avg steps-to-converge, confidence_stop=0.9, n=256

papl_vs_control.interpretation: Identical exact-match, ~0.55 fewer steps clean / ~0.68 fewer aug than control -> the predicted certainty-forcing speedup at zero accuracy cost.

provenance.transformers: 4.49.0 (pinned <5; USE_TF=0 to skip TF/Keras-3 probe on the box)
provenance.attention: SDPA (flash-attn not installed; fine, run is short)

usage.inference: Architecture-identical to base: AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained('diffusion-sql-modernbert-papl') then the existing src/denoising.py denoise_steps loop. No inference-code changes; only the weights differ.
usage.stacks_with: DOS dependency-ordering (denoise_steps strategy='dependency') is orthogonal and can layer on top.

related_files.papl_results.json: raw metrics for this arm (this dir)
related_files.bench_results.json: DONE (in repo root). Frontier benchmark across base/tau_0/tau_0.3. Findings: (1) tau_0.3 uses ~5-7% fewer steps than base at every confidence_stop threshold (frontier shifts left), reproduced at n=512 + on augmented. (2) Zero accuracy gain - all three ~0.293 exact-match. (3) At FIXED step budgets base >= both finetuned arms, so PAPL's speedup is purely an early-stop/certainty-forcing artifact, NOT better quality-per-compute; the 2-epoch finetune slightly eroded fixed-budget quality vs base. Conclusion: PAPL is a modest latency win that ONLY materializes with adaptive confidence_stop, at no accuracy gain.

caveats: tau=0.3 / lr 2e-5 / 2 epochs are A/B settings, not necessarily the optimal prod recipe.
Gain is ~5% fewer steps at equal accuracy; verify it holds / amplifies via the frontier benchmark before committing to prod.
Eval is generation exact-match on gretel synthetic SQL (string match after normalize); execution-accuracy on a real DB would be a stronger prod signal.
